title: Jehoahaz and Jehoash of Israel

questions.question: Who reigned over Israel in Samaria after Jehu?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:1 (ESV): "...Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria..."

questions.question: Who oppressed Israel during the days of Jehoahaz?
options: Hazael king of Syria and Ben-hadad his son
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael king of Syria and Ben-hadad his son
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:3 (ESV): "...and he gave them continually into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael."

questions.question: What happened when Jehoahaz sought the favor of the Lord?
options: The Lord listened to him and gave Israel a savior
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord listened to him and gave Israel a savior
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:4-5 (ESV): "Then Jehoahaz sought the favor of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him... Therefore the LORD gave Israel a savior..."

questions.question: What final act did Elisha perform for King Joash (Jehoash)?
options: He prophesied victory over Syria using arrows
questions.correctAnswer: He prophesied victory over Syria using arrows
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:15-19 (ESV): "And Elisha said to him, 'Take a bow and arrows'... 'The arrow of the LORD's victory... over Syria!'"

questions.question: What miracle happened at Elisha's tomb?
options: A dead man came to life when he touched Elisha's bones
questions.correctAnswer: A dead man came to life when he touched Elisha's bones
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:21 (ESV): "...and as soon as the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood on his feet."

questions.question: How many times did Joash strike the ground with the arrows?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:18 (ESV): "...And he struck three times and stopped."

questions.question: Why was Elisha angry with Joash?
options: Because he should have struck five or six times
Because he didn't strike hard enough
questions.correctAnswer: Because he should have struck five or six times
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:19 (ESV): "Then the man of God was angry with him and said, 'You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck down Syria until you had made an end of it...'"

questions.question: How large was the army left to Jehoahaz?
options: Fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand footmen
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand footmen
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:7 (ESV): "For there was not left to Jehoahaz an army of more than fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand footmen..."

questions.question: Who succeeded Jehoahaz?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:9 (ESV): "So Jehoahaz slept with his fathers... and Joash his son reigned in his place."

questions.question: Who succeeded Hazael as king of Syria?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:24 (ESV): "Hazael king of Syria died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place."

questions.question: What did Joash recover from Ben-hadad?
options: The cities that Hazael had taken from his father
questions.correctAnswer: The cities that Hazael had taken from his father
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:25 (ESV): "Then Jehoash... took again from Ben-hadad... the cities that he had taken from Jehoahaz..."

questions.question: What bands invaded the land in the spring?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:20 (ESV): "So Elisha died... Now bands of Moabites used to invade the land in the spring of the year."

questions.question: Why did the Lord not destroy Israel yet?
options: Because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: Because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:23 (ESV): "...because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them..."

questions.question: Did Jehoahaz depart from the sins of Jeroboam?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:2 (ESV): "He did what was evil... and followed the sins of Jeroboam... he did not depart from them."

key_verse_text: But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them, and he turned toward them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, nor has he cast them from his presence until now. (ESV)
